title: Administration of Justice Correctional Technologies
award: Certificate of Achievement: 18  or greater semester(or 27  or greater quarter) u

program.section_heading: Correctional Technologies - Certificate of Achievement: Miramar
outcomes: Analyze and evaluate the role of criminal sanctions in recidivism rates and the rehabilitation process of offenders.
Use information of crime scene management and investigation, forensics analysis and information technology to conduct rudimentary criminal investigations.
Relate knowledge from several employment areas such as pre-employment testing, physical requirements, psychological evaluations and social factors.
Demonstrate knowledge of the California Penal Code, the California Commission on Peace Officer Standards and Training regulations and appropriate department policies and procedures.
Understand the three components of the criminal justice system and how they interrelate.

notes: ADJU 162 (Criminal Investigation, 3 units) is listed as required in the catalog but is not on the closed list; recorded as a catalog addition.
Catalog states 'Semester Units: 29.5' and 'Total Units: 29.5' for the requirements.

The summary describes the overall Administration of Justice program (Law Enforcement, Investigations, Court Support Services, Contemporary Police Technologies, Correctional Technologies) as training areas rather than named careers; careers left empty. 'Corrections officers' appears only in the ADJU 323A course description and was not recorded.
Outcomes are printed for the Correctional Technologies Program; the lead-in 'Students who complete the Correctional Technologies Program will be able to:' was omitted.
